label: prf:quantum-dilogarithm-stratified
html:
Proof of partition-depth stratification of \Phi_q.

Step 1 (Frobenius dual decomposition of Z(A)). By curvature-rank stratification — together with the partition-vs-word identification this proof itself flags as unestablished at Step 3 below, and which is not supplied by that proposition — the centre Z(A) = \bigoplus_{\lambda \vdash n} R \cdot e_\lambda admits the GB-depth grading Z(A) = \bigoplus_{k \geq 0} Z^{(k)}(A). The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle = \int_A a \cdot b restricts to Z(A) as a non-degenerate bilinear form, and the depth strata Z^{(k)}(A) are mutually orthogonal under this pairing (Frobenius duality of strata "§Frobenius duality of strata"):

  \langle Z^{(k)}(A),\, Z^{(\ell)}(A) \rangle \;=\; 0
  \qquad \text{whenever } k \neq \ell .

Corrected, and the correction repairs Step 4 rather than breaking it. This displayed condition read "whenever k + \ell \neq N", followed by "the self-dual pairing Z^{(k)} \times Z^{(N-k)} \to R is the Poincaré duality of curvature-rank strata" — an anti-diagonal duality, imported from prf:spectral-sequence-collapse "§Frobenius duality of strata", where the same claim has now been refuted in place.

The strata here are spans of central primitive idempotents, and distinct idempotents annihilate each other: for any linear functional \varphi, \varphi(e_\lambda e_\mu) = \varphi(\delta_{\lambda\mu} e_\lambda). So the pairing on that basis is \mathrm{diag}(\tau(e_\lambda)) — diagonal, with every stratum self-dual and every distinct pair annihilating. Measured exactly in \mathbb{Q}(q) at n = 3 on the corpus's own idempotents: all six off-diagonal entries identically 0, diagonal nonzero, completeness self-test \sum_\lambda \tau(e_\lambda) = 1 (centre_frobenius_pairing_is_diagonal_probe.py).

Step 4 needs the diagonal form and does not follow from the anti-diagonal one. It argues that \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) \in Z^{(k)}(A) pairs to zero with any T_w whose Z^{(k)}-projection vanishes. That is precisely \langle Z^{(k)}, Z^{(\ell)}\rangle = 0 for k \neq \ell. Under the old anti-diagonal condition the pairing was licensed to be non-zero at \ell = N - k, so Step 4's truncation did not follow from Step 1 as written whenever N - k \leq k_\star(T_w). The correction closes that hole.

Still open, and not repaired here: Step 4 pairs a central \phi_q^{(k)} against a general T_w \in A, not against a central element, so "T_w has zero projection on Z^{(k)}" has to be read as a statement about T_w's Wedderburn blocks. That reading is plausible — e_\lambda central idempotent gives \tau(e_\lambda a) = \tau(e_\lambda a e_\lambda) — but it is not stated in the block, and it is a different question from the one corrected here. Analysis: docs/audits/2026-08-26-frobenius-duality-of-strata-is-diagonal.md.

where N is the maximal GB-depth in Z(A), retained below only as the top of the depth range. The pairing Z^{(k)} \times Z^{(k)} \to R is non-degenerate on each stratum separately — each stratum is self-dual, and there is no Poincaré-type pairing across distinct strata.

Step 2 (existence of \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i)). By cor: quantum dilogarithm, the level-i torsion-volume contribution to the mass is \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) = \Phi_q(z_i). Since the mass functional is centre-valued by categorical mass = Markov trace, the \Phi_q(z_i)-action on Z(A) via the Markov pairing factors through Z(A). Decomposing along the depth grading,

  \Phi_q(z_i) \cdot \mathrm{id}_{Z(A)}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{k \geq 0} \Phi_q(z_i) \cdot \mathrm{proj}_{Z^{(k)}(A)}.

Define \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) := \mathrm{proj}_{Z^{(k)}(A)}(\Phi_q(z_i)) as the depth-k projection of the Frobenius dual.

Step 3 (cyclotomic factors \leftrightarrow depth-k partitions). The cyclotomic factor (1 - q^{-k} z_i)^{-1} in \Phi_q(z_i) has its pole locus at z_i = q^k. We identify this locus with the depth-k centre stratum Z^{(k)}(A) via the q-content / hook-length structure:

(a) The q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight is w_\lambda(q) = \dim_q^2 V_\lambda / [n]_q! (distinct from the classical Plancherel measure w_\lambda(1) = (\dim V_\lambda)^2/n! — the two coincide at q = 1; see prop:plancherel-weight-boundedness), where \dim_q V_\lambda = [n]_q! \,/\, \prod_{\square \in \lambda} [h(\square)]_q and [h]_q = (q^h - q^{-h})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric quantum integer (Hoefsmit pipeline).

(b) The hook lengths h(\square) for \square \in \lambda encode the partition's depth in the GB filtration. Here \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) = \max_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square) (the partition's maximum hook length) is a definition — it is QOU.BraidKnot.gbDepth, the supremum of the hook length over the cells of \lambda — not a consequence of curvature-rank stratification, which stratifies J^{\,r}/J^{\,r+1} by the curvature rank r(T_w) of words and mentions no partition. The two are different indexings of depth, and the reading of \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) as the minimal number of R_H, R_{YB} rewrites needed to put any element of the \lambda-isotypic component in NF is the identification of the partition grading with the word filtration, which that proposition does not supply.

(c) Therefore \dim_q V_\lambda has a factor of [k]_q in its hook-length expansion exactly when \lambda contains a box with h(\square) = k, equivalently \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) \geq k. Under the substitution z_i \to q^k, the factor [k]_q vanishes — \dim_q V_\lambda(q)\big|_{z_i = q^k} has a zero, and the corresponding w_\lambda^{-1} specialisation has a pole.

(d) The Markov-trace generating function for the centre is the formal series F_n(z) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q^{-1}(V_\lambda) \cdot z^{|\lambda|}, and its expansion as an infinite product in z is F_n(z) = \prod_{k \geq 1} (1 - q^{-k} z)^{-c_k(n)} \cdot u_n(q) where c_k(n) = \#\{\lambda \vdash n : \max\text{-hook}(\lambda) = k\} and u_n(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] is a unit. The exponent c_k(n) counts depth-exactly-k partitions; the factor (1 - q^{-k} z)^{-c_k(n)} contributes the depth-k stratum of Z(A).

(e) The single-stratum factor (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1} in \Phi_q is the c_k = 1 specialisation of (d) — applicable when each depth-k stratum is one-dimensional or when factoring over irreducible strata. For the brane-tower, each exceptional divisor p_i contributes one (1 - q^{-k} z_i)^{-1} per depth k, and the full \Phi_q(z_i) = \prod_k (1 - q^{-k} z_i)^{-1} is the universal generating function over all depths.

(f) Combining (a)–(e): the partial product \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) = \prod_{j=1}^{k}(1-q^{-j}z_i)^{-1} generates exactly the contributions from depths 1, 2, \ldots, k, and the truncation increment \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) - \Phi_q^{[\leq k-1]}(z_i) is the depth-exactly-k generator. Identifying this with the Frobenius dual \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) from Step 2 (modulo orthogonal strata) gives

  \Phi_q^{[\leq k]}(z_i) - \Phi_q^{[\leq k-1]}(z_i)
  \;\equiv\; \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) \pmod{\bigoplus_{\ell \neq k} Z^{(\ell)}(A)}.

Step 4 (Frobenius truncation for T_w). For T_w \in H_n(R, q) with NF support depth k_\star(T_w) = \max_{\lambda \in \mathrm{supp}(T_w)} \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda), T_w has zero projection on Z^{(k)}(A) for every k > k_\star(T_w) by definition of k_\star. By Step 3, \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i) \in Z^{(k)}(A), so

  \bigl\langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i),\, T_w \bigr\rangle \;=\; 0
  \qquad \text{for } k > k_\star(T_w).

The Frobenius-paired sum truncates:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{k = 0}^{\infty} \bigl\langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i),\, T_w \bigr\rangle
  \;=\;
  \sum_{k = 0}^{k_\star(T_w)} \bigl\langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i),\, T_w \bigr\rangle
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr).

The second equality uses depth orthogonality (Step 1); the third uses Step 3's identification of the partial product with the \bigoplus_{j \leq k_\star(T_w)} Z^{(j)}-content. \square

Open: canonical bound. The proof above is a Frobenius-paired equality, not a canonical identity. It says the Frobenius-pairing of \Phi_q(z_i) with T_w equals the Frobenius-pairing of \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i) with T_w. To conclude that the canonical mass formula evaluated with \Phi_q replaced by \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]} gives the same answer, one needs the projections \mathrm{proj}_{Z^{(k)}}(\Phi_q(z_i)) to be uniformly bounded as |z_i| \to q — equivalently, no spurious analytic mass leaks into Z^{(k)}(A) from the divergent infinite product. Establishing this uniform bound is the conjectural target of z-Habiro completion and the open part of \Phi_q categorical truncation.

The argument above is solid as a categorical (Frobenius-paired) identity but does not by itself rule out that the infinite analytic product diverges at |z_i| = q in a way that the finite Frobenius truncation does not capture in real-valued terms. Step 3's identification (a)–(f) reduces the cyclotomic-factor / depth-stratum correspondence to the standard q-content / hook-length formula plus curvature-rank stratification §Step 3 (GB-depth = max hook length), so the structural identification is now explicit — but "explicit" here means written down, not established. The citation does not supply the identification; the passage above, at "not a consequence of [curvature-rank stratification] ... which ... mentions no partition", states the position of this proof. The remaining open piece in Step 3 is (d)'s product expansion F_n(z) = \prod_k (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-c_k(n)} \cdot u_n(q): the existence of such an expansion follows from finiteness of \dim_q^{-1} as a Laurent polynomial and unique factorisation in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}][z], but the explicit identification of the exponents c_k(n) with \#\{\lambda : \max\text{-hook} = k\} requires verification on small cases (D's H_6 and {}^3\mathrm{He}'s H_9 are tractable computations).
